import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def mergeSort_precond (v : List Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
def merge2 : List Int → List Int → List Int
  | [], ys => ys
  | x :: xs, [] => x :: xs
  | x :: xs, y :: ys =>
      if x ≤ y then x :: merge2 xs (y :: ys) else y :: merge2 (x :: xs) ys
termination_by xs ys => xs.length + ys.length
decreasing_by
  all_goals simp only [List.length_cons]
  all_goals omega

theorem perm_cons_middle (a : Int) : ∀ (l r : List Int), (a :: (l ++ r)).Perm (l ++ a :: r)
  | [], r => List.Perm.refl _
  | b :: l, r =>
      (List.Perm.swap b a (l ++ r)).trans ((perm_cons_middle a l r).cons b)

theorem merge2_perm : ∀ (xs ys : List Int), (merge2 xs ys).Perm (xs ++ ys)
  | [], ys => by
      simp only [merge2, List.nil_append]
      all_goals exact List.Perm.refl _
  | x :: xs, [] => by
      simp only [merge2, List.append_nil]
      all_goals exact List.Perm.refl _
  | x :: xs, y :: ys => by
      simp only [merge2]
      split_ifs with hxy
      · exact (merge2_perm xs (y :: ys)).cons x
      · exact ((merge2_perm (x :: xs) ys).cons y).trans (perm_cons_middle y (x :: xs) ys)
termination_by xs ys => xs.length + ys.length
decreasing_by
  all_goals simp only [List.length_cons]
  all_goals omega

theorem merge2_mem {a : Int} {xs ys : List Int} (h : a ∈ merge2 xs ys) :
    a ∈ xs ∨ a ∈ ys := by
  have h2 := (merge2_perm xs ys).mem_iff.mp h
  exact List.mem_append.mp h2

theorem merge2_sorted : ∀ (xs ys : List Int),
    List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) xs → List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) ys → List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) (merge2 xs ys)
  | [], ys => by
      intro _ hy
      simpa only [merge2] using hy
  | x :: xs, [] => by
      intro hx _
      simpa only [merge2] using hx
  | x :: xs, y :: ys => by
      intro hx hy
      rw [List.sorted_cons] at hx hy
      simp only [merge2]
      split_ifs with hxy
      · rw [List.sorted_cons]
        refine ⟨?_, merge2_sorted xs (y :: ys) hx.2 (List.sorted_cons.mpr hy)⟩
        intro b hb
        rcases merge2_mem hb with h | h
        · exact hx.1 b h
        · rcases List.mem_cons.mp h with rfl | h
          · exact hxy
          · exact le_trans hxy (hy.1 b h)
      · have hyx : y ≤ x := le_of_not_le hxy
        rw [List.sorted_cons]
        refine ⟨?_, merge2_sorted (x :: xs) ys (List.sorted_cons.mpr hx) hy.2⟩
        intro b hb
        rcases merge2_mem hb with h | h
        · rcases List.mem_cons.mp h with rfl | h
          · exact hyx
          · exact le_trans hyx (hx.1 b h)
        · exact hy.1 b h
termination_by xs ys => xs.length + ys.length
decreasing_by
  all_goals simp only [List.length_cons]
  all_goals omega

def msort : List Int → List Int
  | [] => []
  | [x] => [x]
  | x :: y :: t =>
      merge2 (msort ((x :: y :: t).take ((t.length + 2) / 2)))
             (msort ((x :: y :: t).drop ((t.length + 2) / 2)))
termination_by l => l.length
decreasing_by
  all_goals simp only [List.length_take, List.length_drop, List.length_cons]
  all_goals first
    | exact lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.min_le_left _ _) (by omega)
    | omega
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definitions
def mergeSort (v : List Int) (h_precond : mergeSort_precond v) : List Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  msort v
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def mergeSort_postcond (v : List Int) (result : List Int) (h_precond : mergeSort_precond v) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
   List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) result ∧ result.Perm v
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem msort_perm : ∀ (l : List Int), (msort l).Perm l
  | [] => by
      simp only [msort]
      all_goals exact List.Perm.refl _
  | [x] => by
      simp only [msort]
      all_goals exact List.Perm.refl _
  | x :: y :: t => by
      simp only [msort]
      have h1 := msort_perm ((x :: y :: t).take ((t.length + 2) / 2))
      have h2 := msort_perm ((x :: y :: t).drop ((t.length + 2) / 2))
      have h3 := merge2_perm (msort ((x :: y :: t).take ((t.length + 2) / 2)))
                             (msort ((x :: y :: t).drop ((t.length + 2) / 2)))
      have h4 := h1.append h2
      rw [List.take_append_drop] at h4
      exact h3.trans h4
termination_by l => l.length
decreasing_by
  all_goals simp only [List.length_take, List.length_drop, List.length_cons]
  all_goals first
    | exact lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.min_le_left _ _) (by omega)
    | omega

theorem msort_sorted : ∀ (l : List Int), List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) (msort l)
  | [] => by
      simp only [msort]
      exact List.sorted_nil
  | [x] => by
      simp only [msort]
      exact List.sorted_singleton x
  | x :: y :: t => by
      simp only [msort]
      exact merge2_sorted (msort ((x :: y :: t).take ((t.length + 2) / 2)))
                          (msort ((x :: y :: t).drop ((t.length + 2) / 2)))
                          (msort_sorted ((x :: y :: t).take ((t.length + 2) / 2)))
                          (msort_sorted ((x :: y :: t).drop ((t.length + 2) / 2)))
termination_by l => l.length
decreasing_by
  all_goals simp only [List.length_take, List.length_drop, List.length_cons]
  all_goals first
    | exact lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.min_le_left _ _) (by omega)
    | omega
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem mergeSort_postcond_satisfied (v : List Int) (h_precond : mergeSort_precond v) :
    mergeSort_postcond v (mergeSort v h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  exact ⟨msort_sorted v, msort_perm v⟩
  -- !benchmark @end proof

## Analysis

**Implementation.** I implement a classic merge sort:

- `merge2 xs ys` merges two lists, recursing with measure `xs.length + ys.length`.
- `msort l` handles `[]` and `[x]` directly, and otherwise splits `l` into `l.take n` / `l.drop n` with `n = length/2`, recursively sorts, and merges. Termination uses `l.length`, needing `0 < n < length` (true since `length ≥ 2`).

**Correctness.**

1. `merge2_perm : (merge2 xs ys) ~ xs ++ ys`, proved by the same recursion; in the "else" branch we need `y :: (xs' ++ ys) ~ xs' ++ y :: ys`, which I prove as a separate structural lemma `perm_cons_middle` (avoiding fragile unification with `List.perm_middle`).
2. `merge2_mem`: membership in a merge implies membership in one of the inputs (via the permutation).
3. `merge2_sorted`: if both inputs are sorted so is the merge; head bound is discharged using `merge2_mem`, the head bounds of the inputs, and transitivity (using `le_of_not_le` in the else branch).
4. `msort_perm` uses `merge2_perm`, `Perm.append` and `take_append_drop`.
5. `msort_sorted` uses `merge2_sorted` with the two recursive results.

Termination goals are discharged by `simp only [length_take, length_drop, length_cons]` followed by `omega` (using `Nat.min_le_left` for the `take` case to avoid `min` in `omega`).
